business_problem: IBM sellers and Business Partners needed a faster, more scalable way to generate reliable product pricing because manual quote assessments relied too heavily on personal experience, incomplete data, and lengthy approval chains.
solution_summary: IBM's CIO Pricing Systems IT team, Chief Analytics Office, and IBM Research co-developed the Cognitive Pricing Analytics solution to embed machine-learning-driven pricing recommendations directly into seller quoting workflows. The system combines years of IBM transactional history with customer buying patterns, geographic context, product strategy, currency conversion, inflation data, and negotiation history so regression-based models can estimate price sensitivity for each quote. Once a seller configures a quote, the solution returns an AI-driven optimal price and routes it through business rules for rapid approval. This closes the loop inside the existing quoting tools instead of forcing sellers to collect data across legacy and third-party systems by hand. The result is a decision-support layer that turns fragmented pricing data into actionable guidance and shortens the time required to produce a defensible, high-confidence quote at scale.

solution_components.name: Cognitive Pricing Analytics
solution_components.role: Integrates with seller quoting tools to score price sensitivity and recommend an optimal quote using machine learning.

data_flow: Quote details flow from the seller's quoting tool into Cognitive Pricing Analytics, the solution combines historical sales, customer, market, and negotiation data to run regression-based models, and the recommended price returns to the workflow for rapid approval.
business_outcome: IBM shortened quote approval paths, improved pricing confidence, and created an explainable AI foundation for modernizing its sales-pricing process across more business units.
